root_cause_label: Insufficient CoreWars domain expertise to design a Snake-defeating warrior
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent lacked domain expertise to counter Snake's imp-spiral hybrid, producing only superficial replicator variants (AdaptivePaper, HybridWarrior, ClearingPaper, ImprovedPaper) that consistently scored 0-3% against Snake, while six consecutive str_replace failures in the final steps consumed the remaining budget and prevented testing of the HybridBomber design.
t_err_evidence: Step 9 planning logs the strategic decision to build a 'quick replicator with anti-vampire mechanisms', choosing a replication-only approach without recognizing that Snake's imp-spiral requires a fundamentally different counter (e.g., a dedicated imp-killer or stone component). All subsequent designs are variants of this same flawed strategy.
t_commit_evidence: Step 32 analysis shows Snake still at 3% after the ClearingPaper iteration; the agent pivots again to 'ImprovedPaper' (a cosmetically different replicator), exhausting creative alternatives. Given the agent's actual behavior of minor parameter tweaking followed by stuck str_replace failures (steps 43-48), failure was now locked in.
t_surface_evidence: Step 14 test shows '0 73 27' against Snake (0 wins out of 100), the first observable signal that the replication strategy cannot beat Snake at any required threshold.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked CoreWars domain knowledge about how to counter an imp-spiral-vampire hybrid like Snake. It correctly identified that paper/replicators beat simpler opponents but never learned that Snake requires a different strategy class (e.g., a fast core-clear, anti-imp mechanism, or stone component). All design iterations remained within the same ineffective replicator family.
forewarning_evidence: Step 11 result vs Stone (29 wins, 71%) is already below the required threshold. Step 14 shows 0 wins against Snake. Step 15 shows 0 wins against G2-Clear. These signals all predate t_commit at step 32.
